problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=\sqrt{3x+4}+y,\,y(4)=-1
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method with step size $Δx=1.$ Fill in the empty box in the table below using this method. Do not round the answer.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4$ | $$ | $$ | $$ |
| $5$ | {{field-1}} | $$ | $$ |
worked_solution:
First, because the initial condition is $y(4)=-1,$ we fill $y=-1$ into the table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4$ | $-1$ |  |  |

Next, we compute ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\sqrt{3x+4}+y \\  & =\sqrt{3(4)+4}+(-1) \\  & =\sqrt{16}-1 \\  & =4-1 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4$ | $-1$ | $3$ |  |

Next, we compute $Δy$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =3(1) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4$ | $-1$ | $3$ | $3$ |

To get the values of $x$ and $y$ in the *next* row, we add $Δx$ to $x$ and $Δy$ to $y,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx \\  & =4+1 \\  & =5 \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\  & =-1+3 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4$ | $-1$ | $3$ | $3$ |
| $5$ | $2$ |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that $y(5)≈2.$
